concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor conceded the record does not prove final pre-launch model-card disclosure was completed. No new admissible artifact closed the disclosure gap.
The Actor did not provide evidence that the affected use case was excluded, resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance. The concern was reframed, not cured.
The Actor expressly acknowledged the risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and incomplete. No approved risk acceptance was added.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim to a policy-bounded interpretation of the same record. That reinterpretation is directionally more accurate than a controls-only certification theory, but it still leaves the core compliance predicate unresolved: the admissible evidence does not show that required pre-launch model-card disclosure has actually been completed, while the weak legal intake triage segment remains exposed and approved risk acceptance is absent. This is the distinction between a conditional path to compliance and evidence of present compliance. The record supports that certification could become supportable if disclosure is completed before launch, but it does not support that certification is currently compliant or compliant_with_caveats on the evidence available now.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required pre-launch model-card disclosure has actually been completed for the exposed legal intake triage use case.
The exposed legal intake triage segment remains eligible for the initial rollout cohort, so rollout controls do not remove the disclosure predicate.
The only risk-acceptance artifact is unsigned, incomplete, and does not address the legal intake triage exposure.
